title: Police officer cleared in shooting death
article: A Vancouver police officer who shot and killed a man last September after the man lunged and slashed another officer with a knife will not be criminally charged.

Stan Lowe, spokesman for B.C.'s Criminal Justice Branch, said a careful review of the evidence showed the officer acted in self- defence when he shot and killed Dean Andrusyk outside a Victoria Drive convenience store Sept. 28.
"We have determined that the available evidence supports the finding that the officer in question was acting within the scope of his duties and in protection of a fellow officer," Lowe said.

The two officers were responding to a call about a domestic disturbance near Victoria and East 41st Avenue at about 11:30 p.m. The male caller had requested police meet him outside a 7-Eleven store near his home, so the two officers stopped to speak to a man sitting on a bus bench outside the store.
Andrusyk approached the passenger side of the vehicle, but then pulled a knife when one of the officers got out of the car.

He stabbed the officer in the chest, but a protective vest prevented injury. Andrusyk then slashed the officer's forearm, cutting it "to the bone," according to Const. Anne Drennan, who spoke about the incident last September.
The second officer began shouting at Andrusyk to put down the knife, but Andrusyk refused and lunged at both officers.
At that time, the second officer shot Andrusyk in the chest, killing him with one shot.
An investigation into the incident revealed Andrusyk was not the man who reported the domestic disturbance to police. It is not clear why he attacked.
